title: NLX2500 SS Tool Post Calibration
reference_docs: Mori Seiki / DMG MORI NLX2500SY/700 Operation & Maintenance Manual (sub-spindle tool-eye sensor-position parameters 2097X / 2098X / 2097Z / 2098Z). Machine record: data/cnc-machines.json (NLX2500, SN NL254140428).
remarks: Run after replacing the sub-spindle tool setter disc/contact post, or after any setter crash. The removable sub-spindle tool-eye arm's four measuring surfaces are defined by paired parameters: X = 2097X & 2098X, Z = 2097Z & 2098Z. X error is diametral (convert to mm, divide by 2 = radial correction). Add/subtract direction for X should be field-verified once and recorded on this procedure. Always record the existing parameter values before changing so they can be reverted.
objective: correctly calibrate the sub-spindle tool setter (removable tool-eye arm) on the Mori Seiki NLX2500SY/700 after the tool setter disc/contact post has been replaced, by re-teaching the sensor-position parameters (2097X / 2098X / 2097Z / 2098Z) so that tools measured on the sub-spindle read true.
overview: Replacing the tool setter disc/contact post physically relocates the four measuring surfaces of the sub-spindle tool-eye. Until the stored sensor-position parameters are re-taught, every tool measured on the sub-spindle side will be off by the amount the post moved. This procedure re-establishes those parameters using a mic-verified reference tool and a measure-error to adjust-parameter loop, then verifies to tolerance. Perform with SINGLE BLOCK enabled and rapid/feed override turned down.

tasks.name: Task 1 - Preparation and safety
steps: Confirm the new tool setter disc/contact post is fully seated and torqued on the removable sub-spindle arm.
Enable SINGLE BLOCK; turn rapid override and feed override down. Keep one hand near FEED HOLD throughout.
On the sensor-position parameter screen, RECORD the current values of 2097X, 2098X, 2097Z, and 2098Z on paper so they can be reverted if needed.
Deploy the removable sub-spindle tool-eye arm and confirm it is seated and clear of the turret path.

tasks.name: Task 2 - Establish a reference (truth) tool
steps: Chuck a test bar in the SUB-SPINDLE.
Face the bar; set the reference tool's Z geometry offset to the faced surface.
Turn the OD a short distance, retract without moving X, and measure the diameter with a micrometer.
Set the reference tool's X geometry offset from the measured diameter. Mic-verify. This tool is now the calibration reference.

tasks.name: Task 3 - Measure the reference tool on the setter
steps: With the reference tool selected, touch it off on the sub-spindle setter using the normal tool-measurement function.
Write down the X (and Z) geometry value the setter reports for the reference tool.

tasks.name: Task 4 - Cut a test part and calculate the error
steps: With the reference tool, take a skim finish cut on the sub-spindle part.
Micrometer the actual cut DIAMETER (X) and the actual FACE/length (Z).
X error = setter-reported diameter minus mic'd diameter. Convert to millimeters if needed, then DIVIDE BY 2 to get the radial correction.
Z error = setter-reported face minus mic'd face (direct value, no halving).

tasks.name: Task 5 - Correct the sensor-position parameters
steps: Navigate to the sub-spindle tool-eye sensor-position parameters per the machine book (SYSTEM to SETUP to AXIS, page to the 209x block).

X axis: shift BOTH 2097X and 2098X by the Task 4 radial value. If the test part measured OVERSIZE add the value; if UNDERSIZE subtract it (verify this sign once on this machine, then record it on this sheet).
Z axis: shift BOTH 2097Z and 2098Z by the Task 4 Z error, using the same oversize/undersize sign logic.
Move both members of each axis pair by the SAME amount - you are translating the re-installed post, not changing its geometry.

tasks.name: Task 6 - Verify and iterate
steps: Repeat Task 3 and Task 4. Because the entire post was replaced, expect 2 to 3 iterations to converge.
Continue until the setter reading agrees with the mic within plus/minus 0.0002 in (plus/minus 0.005 mm) on both axes.
Confirm on a second tool plus a test cut before trusting production offsets.

If X and Z are both far off after one pass, a sign is likely flipped - revert to the recorded values and redo that axis. If it will not converge, the arm is not repeatably seating (mechanical issue), not a parameter issue.
Record the final 2097X / 2098X / 2097Z / 2098Z values and the verified X sign direction on this sheet.
